units.text: A psalm of David, when his son pursues him. Lord, hear my prayer; give ear to my plea in Thy truth. Answer me in Thy righteousness.
Do not enter into judgment with Thy servant, for no one living will be justified before Thee.
For the enemy pursued my soul, brought my life low to the ground, made me sit in dark places like those long dead.
My spirit grew despondent within me; within me my heart was troubled.
We will acknowledge Thee, God; we will acknowledge and call upon Thy name.
I will recount all Thy wonders when I take an appointed time; I will judge uprightness.
The earth and all who inhabit it melted; I established its pillars. Diapsalma.
I said to those acting lawlessly, “Do not act lawlessly,” and to those sinning, “Do not raise a horn;
do not lift your horn on high; do not speak injustice against God.”
For neither from the goings-out nor from the settings, nor from desert mountains,
for God is judge: He humbles this one and raises that one.
For behold, the Lord’s incurable day comes, of wrath and anger, to make the whole inhabited world deserted and destroy its sinners from it.
For heaven’s stars, Orion and all heaven’s array will not give light; it will grow dark as the sun rises, and the moon will not give its light.
I will ordain evils for the whole inhabited world, and for the ungodly their sins; I will destroy the insolence of the lawless and lower the insolence of the proud.
Those left will be more precious than unrefined gold, and a human being more precious than the stone from Souphir.
For heaven will be enraged, and the earth shaken from its foundations through the fury of the Lord Sabaoth’s anger, on the day when His wrath comes upon it.
Will you not know? Will you not hear? Was it not announced to you from the beginning? Did you not know the earth’s foundations?
He holds the earth’s circuit, and its inhabitants are like locusts. He set heaven like a vault and stretched it out like a tent to dwell in.
He gives rulers nothing to rule and made the earth as nothing.
For they will certainly not sow or plant, nor will their root take hold in the earth. He blew on them, and they dried; a storm will carry them away like brushwood.
“Now then, to whom did you liken Me, and shall I be exalted?” said the Holy One.
Lift your eyes on high and see: Who displayed all these? He brings out His array by number and will call all by name. From abundant glory and in strength’s might, nothing escaped you.
Immediately He compelled the disciples to enter a boat and go ahead of Him to the other side, while He dismissed the crowds.
After dismissing the crowds, He went up the mountain privately to pray. When evening came, He was there alone.
The boat was already many stadia from land, battered by the waves, for the wind was against them.
In the fourth watch of the night He came toward them, walking upon the sea.
When the disciples saw Him walking upon the sea, they were troubled and said, “It is an apparition!” They cried out in fear.
Immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, “Take courage; it is I. Do not fear.”
Peter answered Him, “Lord, if it is Thou, command me to come to Thee upon the waters.”
He said, “Come.” Peter got down from the boat, walked upon the waters, and came toward Jesus.
But seeing the strong wind, he became afraid; beginning to sink, he cried out, “Lord, save me!”
Immediately Jesus stretched out His hand, grasped him, and said to him, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”
When they climbed into the boat, the wind ceased.
Those in the boat worshiped Him, saying, “Truly Thou art God’s Son.”
Three things are impossible for me to understand, and the fourth I do not comprehend:
the tracks of a flying eagle, and the ways of a snake upon a rock, and the paths of a seagoing ship, and the ways of a man in youth.
Such is the way of an adulterous woman: when she has acted, she washes herself and says she has done nothing improper.
What did arrogance profit us? And what did wealth with boasting contribute to us?
All those things passed like a shadow and like a report rushing by;
like a ship passing through surging water, whose trace cannot be found after it has crossed, nor the path of its keel among the waves;

or like a bird that has flown through the air: no sign of its passage is found. It crossed the light air, lashed by the beat of its pinions and split by the force of its rushing wings; and afterward no sign of its passage was found in it;
or like an arrow shot at a target: the air it cut immediately flowed back into itself, so that its course could not be known:
so we also were born and vanished, and had no sign of virtue to show, but were consumed in our wickedness.”

For the hope of an ungodly person is like dust borne by wind, and like fine frost driven by a storm; like smoke it was dispersed by wind, and like the memory of a guest who stayed one day it passed away.
Your apostasy will discipline you, and your evil will rebuke you. Know and see that abandoning Me is bitter for you, says the Lord your God; and I took no pleasure in you, says the Lord your God.

For long ago you shattered your yoke and tore apart your bonds, and said, I will not be enslaved, but I will go upon every high hill and beneath every shady tree; there I will abandon myself to my prostitution.
But I planted you as a fruitful vine, wholly genuine. How have you changed into bitterness, you foreign vine?
Even if you wash with natron and multiply cleansing herb for yourself, you remain stained in your injustices before Me, says the Lord.
How will you say, I was not polluted and did not follow Baal? See your ways in the burial ground and know what you did. Late her voice wailed; her ways
He showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, with the slanderer standing at his right hand to oppose him.
The Lord said to the slanderer, “May the Lord rebuke you, slanderer! May the Lord, who chose Jerusalem, rebuke you! Look, is this not like a brand pulled from fire?”
Joshua was clothed in filthy garments and standing before the angel.
He answered and said to those standing before him, “Remove the filthy garments from him.” He said to him, “Look, I have taken away your lawless deeds; clothe him in a robe reaching to the feet,
and put a clean turban on his head.” They clothed him in garments and put a clean turban on his head, while the angel of the Lord stood by.
And he took up his parable and said: Rise, Balak, and hear! Listen as a witness, son of Zippor!
God is not as a man, to be led astray, nor as a son of man, to be threatened; having spoken, shall He not act? Shall He speak, and not abide by it?
Behold, I have been taken up to bless. I will bless and certainly will not reverse it.
There shall be no toil in Jacob, neither shall distress be seen in Israel; the Lord his God is with him; the glories of rulers are in him.
God brought them out of Egypt; his glory is as that of a one-horned beast.
There is no omen-taking in Jacob and no divination in Israel. At the appointed time it shall be said to Jacob and Israel what God will accomplish.
Behold, a people will rise like a lion cub and exult like a lion. It will not sleep until it eats prey and drinks the blood of the slain.
Therefore I urge first of all that petitions, prayers, intercessions and thanksgivings be made for all people,
for kings and all who are in high positions, so that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and dignity.
This is good and acceptable before God our Savior,
who wills all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of truth.
For there is one God, and one mediator between God and human beings, the human being Christ Jesus,
who gave Himself as a ransom in exchange for all, the testimony at the proper times.
For this I was appointed a herald and an apostle—I speak truth, I do not lie—a teacher of nations in faith and truth.
If I walk amid affliction, Thou wilt keep me alive; against my enemies’ anger Thou didst stretch out Thy hand, and Thy right hand saved me.
The Lord will repay on my behalf. Lord, Thy mercy is for ever; do not neglect the works of Thy hands.

The Lord said to Samuel, “How long will you mourn over Saul, when I have treated him as nothing so that he should not reign over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and come. I will send you to Jesse, to Bethlehem, for I have seen one among his sons to reign for Me.”
Samuel said, “How can I go? Saul will hear and kill me.” The Lord said, “Take a heifer in your hand and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the Lord.’
Invite Jesse to the sacrifice. I will make known to you what you must do, and you shall anoint the one I name to you.”
Samuel did everything the Lord had spoken to him and came to Bethlehem. The city’s elders were terrified at meeting him and said, “Do you enter in peace, seer?”
He said, “In peace. I have come to sacrifice to the Lord. Consecrate yourselves and rejoice with me today.” He consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.
When they came in, he saw Eliab and said, “Surely His anointed is before the Lord.”

The Lord said to Samuel, “Do not look at his appearance or the bearing of his height, for I have treated him as nothing. God does not see as a human looks: a human looks at the face, but God looks at the heart.”
Jesse called Aminadab, and he passed before Samuel. He said, “The Lord has not chosen this one either.”
Jesse made Shammah pass by. He said, “The Lord has not chosen this one either.”
Jesse made his seven sons pass before Samuel. Samuel said, “The Lord has not chosen among these.”

Samuel said to Jesse, “Are these all the boys?” He said, “There is still the youngest; he is tending the flock.” Samuel said to Jesse, “Send and fetch him, for we will certainly not recline until he comes.”
He sent and brought him. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and good to look upon before the Lord. The Lord said to Samuel, “Rise and anoint David, for this one is good.”
Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him among his brothers. The Lord’s Spirit leaped upon David from that day onward. Samuel rose and went to Armathaim.
A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, Thou becamest our refuge through every generation.
Before the mountains came to be and the earth and inhabited world were formed, from age to age Thou art.
Do not turn a man toward humiliation; and Thou saidst, Return, sons of men.
For a thousand years in Thine eyes are like yesterday, which passed, and a watch in the night.
Their things counted as nothing will be years. In the morning, like green grass, may it pass away;
in the morning may it blossom and pass away; in the evening may it fall, grow hard and dry up.
For the end. A psalm for David. Lord, Thou didst test me and know me.
Thou knewest my sitting and my rising; Thou didst understand my reasonings from afar.
Thou didst trace my path and my measuring cord, and Thou didst foresee all my ways.
For there is no word on my tongue,
behold, Lord, Thou knewest all things, the last and the first; Thou didst form me and place Thy hand upon me.
Thy knowledge was made wondrous beyond me; it grew strong—I cannot reach it.
Where can I go from Thy Spirit, and where can I flee from Thy face?
If I ascend to heaven, Thou art there; if I descend into Hades, Thou art present.
if I take up my wings at dawn and settle at the sea’s farthest reaches,
indeed, even there Thy hand will guide me, and Thy right hand will hold me fast.
And I said, “Then darkness will trample me, and night is light in my delight.”
For darkness will not be dark from Thee, and night will be lit up like day; as its darkness, so also its light.
For Thou didst acquire my kidneys, Lord; Thou didst support me from my mother’s womb.
I will thank Thee, for I was made fearfully wonderful; wondrous are Thy works, and my soul knows very well.
My bone was not hidden from Thee, which Thou madest in secret, and my substance in earth’s lowest places.
Thine eyes saw my unworked substance, and in Thy book all will be written; they will be formed over days, and none among them.
Thy friends were greatly honored by me, God; their beginnings grew very strong.
I will count them, and they will multiply beyond the sand; I awoke, and I am still with Thee.
If Thou dost kill sinners, God— men of blood, turn away from me,
for Thou wilt speak into deliberation; they will take Thy cities into vanity.
Did I not hate those who hate Thee, Lord, and melt away over Thine enemies?
I hated them with complete hatred; they became enemies to me.
Test me, God, and know my heart; examine me and know my paths,
and see whether a way of lawlessness is in me, and guide me in an eternal way.
For the Lord shall judge His people, and be moved concerning His servants; for He saw them weakened, and failing under assault, and exhausted.
And the Lord said, Where are their gods, in whom they trusted,
whose sacrifices’ fat you ate, and whose drink offerings’ wine you drank? Let them arise and help you, and become your protectors.
See, see that I am, and there is no god beside Me. I will put to death, and make alive; I will smite, and I will heal; and there is none that shall deliver out of My hands.
For I will lift My hand unto heaven, and swear by My right hand, and say, I live for ever.
For I will sharpen My sword as lightning, and My hand shall lay hold of judgment; and I will repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Me will I repay.
I will make My arrows drunk with blood, and My sword shall devour flesh, from the blood of the slain and of captives, from the head of the rulers of the enemies.

Rejoice, O heavens, together with Him, and let all the sons of God worship Him; rejoice, O nations, with His people, and let all the angels of God give Him strength; for He avenges the blood of His sons, and shall avenge and repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Him shall He repay; and the Lord shall thoroughly cleanse the land of His people.
There is no one calling on Thy name or remembering to take hold of Thee, because Thou didst turn Thy face away from us and didst hand us over because of our sins.
But now, Lord, Thou art our Father, and we are clay, all the work of Thy hands.
Do not be exceedingly angry with us or remember our sins at the appointed time. And now look, for we are all Thy people.
The city of Thy holy place became a desert; Zion became like a desert, Jerusalem a curse.
This is the book of the origin of heaven and earth, when they came to be, on the day when God made heaven and earth,

and every green plant of the field before it appeared upon the earth, and every plant of the field before it sprang up. For God had not sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to till the ground.
But a spring rose from the earth and watered the whole face of the ground.
And God formed man from the dust of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
And the Lord God planted a garden in Eden, toward the east, and there He placed the man whom He had formed.
And God caused every tree that was beautiful to behold and good for food to spring up from the earth, with the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

And to Adam He said: Because you listened to the voice of your wife and ate from the tree of which alone I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the earth in your labours; in pain you shall eat of it all the days of your life.
Thorns and thistles it shall bring forth for you, and you shall eat the plants of the field.
By the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread, until you return to the earth from which you were taken; for earth you are, and unto earth you shall return.
And Adam called his wife’s name Life, because she was the mother of all the living.
And the Lord God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and clothed them.
I too am a mortal human being, equal to all, and a descendant of the first-formed earthborn man; in a mother’s womb I was sculpted into flesh,
taking form in blood over a time of ten months, from a man’s seed and the pleasure that accompanied sleep.
And when I was born, I drew in the common air and fell upon the earth that shares the same lot, crying as my first sound just like everyone else.
I was brought up in swaddling clothes and attentive care.
For no king had a different beginning of birth;
all have one entrance into life, and the same departure.
I am the man who sees poverty under the rod of His fury against me.
He took me and led me away into darkness, not light.
Indeed, against me He turned His hand all day.
He made my flesh and my skin old; He shattered my bones.
He built against me, surrounded my head and toiled.
He made me dwell in dark places like the dead of ages.
He built against me, and I will not go out; He made my bronze heavy.
Indeed, I will cry and call out; He blocked my prayer.
He built up my roads, blocked my paths and troubled them.
He is a bear lying in wait for me, a lion in hidden places.
He pursued me when I turned away and brought me to a stop; He made me desolate.
He drew His bow and fixed me as a target for a missile.
He drove the arrows of His quiver into my kidneys.
I became a laughingstock to all my people, their psalm all day.
He filled me with bitterness and made me drunk with gall.
He knocked out my teeth with a pebble and fed me ashes.
He drove my soul away from peace; I forgot good things.
I said, “My victory has perished, and my hope from the Lord.”
Through much talking you will not escape sin, but by sparing your lips you will be intelligent.
The tongue of the righteous is fire-tested silver, but the heart of the impious will fail.
The lips of the righteous know lofty things, but fools die in want.
For just as you once disobeyed God, but now received mercy through their disobedience,
so they also now disobeyed, so that through the mercy shown to you they also may now receive mercy.
For God confined all in disobedience so that He might have mercy on all.
O depth of God’s wealth and wisdom and knowledge! How unsearchable His judgments and untraceable His ways!
“For who knew the Lord’s mind? Or who became His counselor?
Or who gave to Him first, and it will be repaid to him?”
Because from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory throughout the ages. Amen.
Who spoke in this way and it came to be? The Lord did not command,
will not calamities and good come from the mouth of the Most High?
Why should a living person grumble, a man concerning his sin?
Our way was searched and examined; let us return to the Lord.
Let us lift our hearts upon our hands to the Exalted One in heaven.
We have sinned and acted godlessly, and Thou wast not propitiated.
Thou didst cover Thyself with fury and drive us away; Thou didst kill without sparing.
Thou didst spread a cloud over Thyself because of prayer,
to close my eyes; Thou didst place us to be rejected among the peoples.
Hear the Lord’s word, rulers of Sodom! Attend to God’s law, people of Gomorrah!
“What is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?” says the Lord. “I am full of burnt offerings of rams; fat of lambs and blood of bulls and male goats I do not desire,
not even if you come to appear before Me. For who demanded these things from your hands? To trample My court,
you will no longer continue. If you bring fine flour, it is futile. Incense is an abomination to Me. Your new moons and sabbaths and a great day I cannot endure; fasting and idleness,
and your new moons and your festivals My soul hates. You have become more than enough for Me; I will no longer let your sins go.
Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves, become clean. Remove the evils from your souls, before My eyes. Stop your evil deeds.
Learn to do good, seek judgment, rescue the wronged. Give judgment for the orphan and vindicate the widow.
Come, let us reason together, says the Lord. Though your sins are like purple-red, I will whiten them like snow; though they are like scarlet, I will whiten them like wool.
If you are willing and listen to Me, you will eat the land’s good things.
But if you are unwilling and do not listen to Me, a sword will devour you, for the Lord’s mouth has spoken these things.”
Therefore thus says the Lord: “Behold, those serving Me will eat, but you will hunger. Those serving Me will drink, but you will thirst. Those serving Me will rejoice, but you will be ashamed.
Behold, those serving Me will exult with joy, but you will cry out because of your heart’s pain and wail from a broken spirit.
For you will leave your name as a surfeit for My chosen ones, but the Lord will put you to death. Those serving Him will be called a new name,

which will be blessed upon earth. For they will bless the true God, and those swearing upon earth will swear by the true God. They will forget their former affliction, and it will not rise into their heart.
For heaven will be new and earth new, and they will never remember former things, nor will those things enter their heart,
but they will find joy and exultation in it. For behold, I am making Jerusalem an exultation and My people joy.
I will exult over Jerusalem and rejoice over My people, and no sound of weeping or crying will ever again be heard in her.
Of David. Do not be provoked to envy by those doing evil, nor envy those committing lawlessness.
For like grass they will quickly dry up, and like green plants they will quickly fall away.
Hope in the Lord and show kindness; settle in the land, and you will be pastured on its wealth.
Delight yourself in the Lord, and He will give you the requests of your heart.
Reveal your way to the Lord; hope in Him, and He will act.
He will bring out your righteousness like light, and your judgment like noon.
Submit to the Lord and beseech Him; do not be provoked to envy by one prospering in his way, by a person committing lawless deeds.
Cease from anger and abandon wrath; do not be provoked to envy so as to act wickedly.
For those doing evil will be destroyed, but those who wait for the Lord will inherit the land.
Go to the ant, sluggard; see its ways and emulate them, and become wiser than it.
For although it has no cultivated field, and has no one forcing it, and is under no master,
it prepares its food in summer and makes abundant provision at harvest.
Or go to the bee and learn how industrious she is, and how nobly she performs her work,
whose labors kings and private people use for health; she is desired by everyone and held in esteem.
Although weak in bodily strength, she was advanced because she honored wisdom.
How long will you remain lying down, sluggard? When will you rise from sleep?
You sleep a little, sit a little, doze a little, and clasp your chest with your hands a little;
then poverty arrives beside you like an evil traveler, and want like a good runner.
And God said, “Let the waters bring forth living creatures that move, and birds that fly above the earth across the firmament of heaven.” And it was so.

And God made the great sea creatures, and every living creature that moves, which the waters brought forth according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that they were good.
And God blessed them, saying, “Grow and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas; and let the birds multiply upon the earth.”
And there was evening, and there was morning: a fifth day.
And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kind: four-footed animals, creeping things, and wild beasts of the earth according to their kind.” And it was so.

And God made the wild beasts of the earth according to their kind, and the cattle according to their kind, and all the creeping things of the earth according to their kinds. And God saw that they were good.

And God said, “Let Us make man in Our image and likeness; and let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, the cattle, all the earth, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.”
And God made man; in the image of God He made him; male and female He made them.

And God blessed them, saying, “Grow and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, all the cattle, all the earth, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.”
Paul stood in the midst of the Areopagus and said, “Men of Athens, I perceive that in every respect you are very religious.
For as I passed through and observed your objects of worship, I also found an altar inscribed, ‘To an unknown god.’ What you worship without knowing, this I proclaim to you.
The God who made the world and everything in it, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in sanctuaries made by hands.
Nor is He served by human hands as though He needed anything, since He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything.
From one He made every nation of humanity to live upon the whole face of the earth, determining their appointed times and the boundaries of their dwelling,
so that they might seek God, if perhaps they might feel their way toward Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.
For in Him we live and move and exist, as even some of your own poets have said, ‘For we too are His offspring.’
Since we are God’s offspring, we ought not to think that the divine nature is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by human art and thought.
Therefore, having overlooked the times of ignorance, God now commands all people everywhere to repent,
because He has fixed a day on which He will judge the inhabited world in righteousness through a Man whom He appointed, giving assurance to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”
Then Daniel went to his house and explained everything to his companions Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

He called for fasting and supplication and for help to be sought from the Lord Most High concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and those with him would not be handed over to destruction with Babylon’s learned men.
Then, in a vision that very night, the king’s mystery was plainly revealed to Daniel. Daniel blessed the Lord Most High,
and cried out, “The name of the great Lord will be blessed for ever, because wisdom and majesty belong to Him.
He changes seasons and times, transfers kings and appoints them, gives wisdom to the wise and understanding to those who possess knowledge,
reveals deep and dark things, knows what is in darkness and what is in light, and with Him is a dwelling.
To Thee, Lord of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because Thou hast given me wisdom and prudence. Now Thou hast shown me everything I requested, to disclose these things to the king.”

Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to kill all Babylonia’s learned men, and said, “Do not destroy Babylonia’s learned men. Bring me to the king, and I will disclose every detail to him.”
On that day I will call My servant Eliakim, son of Chelkias,
clothe him in your robe, give him your crown, and put the power and your stewardship in his hands. He will be like a father to those dwelling in Jerusalem and those dwelling in Judah.
I will give him David’s glory, and he will rule, with no one contradicting.
I will establish him as a ruler in a trustworthy place, and he will become a throne of glory for his father’s house.
Every glorious person in his father’s house, from small to great, will trust in him, and they will hang upon him.
On that day—thus says the Lord Sabaoth—the person established in a trustworthy place will be shaken and fall, and the glory upon him will be removed, because the Lord has spoken.”
In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the deep burst open, and the floodgates of heaven were opened.
And rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On that very day Noah entered the ark, with Shem, Ham, and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah’s wife and the three wives of his sons with him.
And every wild beast according to its kind, all the cattle according to their kind, every creeping thing that moves upon the earth according to its kind, and every bird according to its kind
entered the ark with Noah, two by two of all flesh in which is the breath of life.
Those that entered were male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded Noah. And the Lord God closed the ark from the outside.
And the flood was upon the earth for forty days and forty nights. And the waters increased and lifted the ark, and it rose above the earth.
And the waters prevailed and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark floated upon the waters.
And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth, and covered all the high mountains beneath heaven.
The waters rose fifteen cubits above them and covered all the high mountains.
And all flesh that moved upon the earth died: birds, cattle, wild beasts, every creeping thing that moves upon the earth, and all mankind.
Everything that had the breath of life, everything upon the dry land, died.

And He blotted out every living thing upon the face of the whole earth: mankind, cattle, creeping things, and the birds of heaven. They were blotted out from the earth, and only Noah remained, and those with him in the ark.
And the waters remained high upon the earth for one hundred and fifty days.

And God remembered Noah, and all the wild beasts, all the cattle, all the birds, and all the creeping things that were with him in the ark. And God brought a wind upon the earth, and the waters subsided.
And the fountains of the deep and the floodgates of heaven were closed, and the rain from heaven was restrained.
And the waters steadily withdrew from the earth; after one hundred and fifty days the waters had receded and diminished.
And in the seventh month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the ark rested upon the mountains of Ararat.
And the waters continued to diminish until the tenth month. In the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains appeared.
A vision of Egypt. Behold, the Lord sits upon a light cloud and will come into Egypt; Egypt’s handmade objects will be shaken before Him, and their heart overcome within them.
Egyptians will be roused against Egyptians; each will fight his brother and each his neighbor, city against city and district against district.
The Egyptians’ spirit will be troubled within them, and I will scatter their counsel. They will inquire of their gods, their statues, those speaking from the earth and the belly-speakers.
I will hand Egypt into the hands of harsh human masters, and harsh kings will rule them. Thus says the Lord Sabaoth.
The Egyptians will drink water beside the sea, but the river will fail and dry up.
Rivers and the river’s canals will fail, and every gathering of water dry up, in every marsh of reed and papyrus,
and all the green marsh growth around the river and everything sown by the river will dry up, destroyed by wind.
Fishermen will groan, and all casting a hook into the river will groan; those casting seines and those using casting nets will mourn.
Shame will seize those working split flax and those working fine linen,
and those warping them will be in pain, and all who make beer will be grieved and suffer in their souls.
Tanis’s rulers will be fools; the king’s wise counselors—their counsel will become foolish. How will you say to the king, “We are sons of the discerning, sons of kings from the beginning”?
Where are your wise men now? Let them announce to you and say what the Lord Sabaoth has counseled against Egypt.
Tanis’s rulers failed, and Memphis’s rulers were exalted; they will lead Egypt astray tribe by tribe.
For the Lord mixed for them a spirit of wandering; they led Egypt astray in all their works, as someone wanders while drunk and vomiting.
There will be no work for the Egyptians that will produce a head and tail, a beginning and end.
On that day the Egyptians will be like women in fear and trembling before the Lord Sabaoth’s hand, which He Himself will bring upon them.
The Judeans’ country will become a terror to the Egyptians; whenever anyone names her to them, they will fear because of the counsel the Lord has counseled against her.
The chief cook took Saraias the first priest, Sophonias, son of the second rank, and the three doorpost guards,

and from the city he took one eunuch who supervised the warriors, five men who saw the king’s face who were found in the city, the scribe of the commander of the force who drew up the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land found in the city.
Nabouzardan, the chief cook, took them and led them to the king of Babylon at Deblatha.
The king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Deblatha in Aimath’s land. Judah was deported from its land.
He made rivers a wilderness and outlets of waters thirst,
a fruitful land brine, because of the wickedness of those inhabiting it.
He made a wilderness lakes of waters and waterless land outlets of waters,
and settled hungry people there, and they established a city of habitation,
and sowed fields and planted vineyards and produced a fruitful crop.
He blessed them, and they multiplied greatly, and He did not diminish their livestock.
They became few and suffered harm from the affliction of evils and pain.
Contempt was poured out upon rulers, and He made them wander in an impassable place, not a road.
He helped the poor out of poverty and made families like sheep.
The upright will see and rejoice, and all lawlessness will stop its mouth.
Who is wise and will keep these things, and will they understand the Lord’s mercies?
“Are you not like the children of Ethiopians to Me, children of Israel?” says the Lord. “Did I not bring Israel up from Egypt’s land, the foreigners from Cappadocia and the Syrians from a pit?
Look, the Lord God’s eyes are upon the kingdom of sinners, and I will remove it from the earth’s surface. Yet I will not completely remove Jacob’s house,” says the Lord.
“For look, I am giving a command: I will winnow Israel’s house among all the nations as one winnows in a winnowing basket, and no fragment will fall to the ground.
All the sinners of My people will die by a sword, those who say, ‘Evils certainly will not draw near or come upon us.’
One who refrains from sending forth a harsh word is discerning, and a patient man is intelligent.
Wisdom will be reckoned to a senseless person who asks for wisdom, and someone who makes himself mute will seem intelligent.
My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with acts of favoritism.
For if a man with gold rings and splendid clothing enters your gathering, and a poor person in filthy clothing also enters,
and you pay attention to the one wearing splendid clothing and say, “You sit here in a good place,” but say to the poor person, “You stand, or sit there beneath my footstool,”
have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen those poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?
But you have dishonored the poor person. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into courts?
Do they not blaspheme the good name called over you?
If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.
But if you show favoritism, you commit sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors.
For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one point has become accountable for all of it.
For He who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” Now if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.
So speak and so act as those who are going to be judged through a law of freedom.
For judgment is without mercy to the one who has shown no mercy; mercy triumphs over judgment.
Saul spoke to his son Jonathan and to all his servants about putting David to death. But Saul’s son Jonathan greatly favoured David.
Jonathan told David, saying, “Saul seeks to put you to death. So be on your guard tomorrow morning, hide, and remain concealed.
I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you may be. I will speak about you to my father, see what happens, and report to you.”
Jonathan spoke good things about David to his father Saul and said to him, “Let the king not sin against your servant David, for he has not sinned against you, and his deeds are very good.

He placed his soul in his hand and struck the foreigner, and the Lord brought about a great deliverance. All Israel saw and rejoiced. Why do you sin against innocent blood by putting David to death without cause?”
Saul listened to Jonathan’s voice, and Saul swore, saying, “As the Lord lives, he shall not die.”
Jonathan called David and told him all these words. Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was before him as in former days.
Give ear to my words, Lord; understand my cry.
Attend to the voice of my petition, my King and my God, for unto Thee I will pray, Lord.
In the morning Thou wilt hear my voice; in the morning I will stand before Thee and watch.
For Thou art not a God who desires lawlessness, nor will an evildoer sojourn with Thee.
The lawless will not remain before Thine eyes; Thou didst hate all who work lawlessness.
Thou wilt destroy all who speak falsehood; the Lord abhors a man of bloodshed and deceit.
But I, through the multitude of Thy mercy, will enter Thy house; I will bow toward Thy holy temple in fear of Thee.
The Lord gives me a tongue of instruction, to know the right time when a word must be spoken. He appointed morning for me; He added an ear for me to hear,
and the Lord’s instruction opens my ears. I do not disobey or contradict.
I have given my back to scourges and my cheeks to slaps. I did not turn my face away from the shame of spitting.
The Lord became my helper; therefore I was not abashed. Instead, I set my face like solid rock and knew that I would certainly not be ashamed.
For the One who justified me draws near. Who is bringing a case against me? Let him stand against me together. Who is bringing a case against me? Let him approach me.
Behold, the Lord helps me. Who will harm me? Behold, all of you will grow old like a garment, and it will devour you like a moth.
Who among you fears the Lord? Let him listen to His servant’s voice. Those walking in darkness have no light; trust in the Lord’s name and lean upon God.
Behold, all of you burn fire and strengthen a flame. Walk by your fire’s light and the flame you kindled. These things came to you because of Me; you will fall asleep in sorrow.
Make Thy ways known to me, Lord, and teach me Thy paths.
Guide me into Thy truth and teach me, for Thou art God my Savior, and I waited for Thee the whole day.
Remember Thy compassions, Lord, and Thy mercies, for they are from eternity.
Do not remember the sins of my youth or my acts of ignorance; according to Thy mercy, remember me Thyself, for Thy kindness’ sake, Lord.
The Lord is kind and upright; therefore He will give sinners instruction in the way.
He will guide the meek in judgment; He will teach the meek His ways.
All the Lord’s ways are mercy and truth for those who seek His covenant and His testimonies.
For Thy name’s sake, Lord, Thou wilt be gracious to my sin, for it is great.
Great occupation was created for every person, and a heavy yoke lies upon Adam’s sons, from the day they leave their mother’s womb until the day they return to the mother of all:
their thoughts and fear of heart, anxious expectation, the day of death.
From the one seated upon a glorious throne to the one brought low in earth and ashes,
from the one wearing blue and a crown to the one clothed in raw linen, there are anger, jealousy, trouble, upheaval, fear of death, resentment, and strife.
Even at the time of rest upon a bed, night’s sleep alters his awareness.
He rests a little, almost nothing; then in sleep, as on a day of keeping watch, he is troubled by his heart’s vision, like someone who escaped from battle.
At his time of need he woke, marveling that there was nothing to fear.
As a father has compassion on children, the Lord had compassion on those who fear Him,
for He knew our formation. Remember that we are dust.
A man—his days are like grass; like a flower of the field, so he will flower,
for a wind passed through him, and he will not exist, and he will no longer recognize his place.
But the Lord’s mercy is from eternity to eternity toward those who fear Him, and His righteousness toward children’s children,
to those who keep His covenant and remember His commandments to do them.
“Make known to me, Lord, my limit and the number of my days, what it is, so that I may know what I lack.
Behold, Thou madest my days handbreadths, and my existence is as nothing before Thee. Yet all things are vanity—every living person. Diapsalma.
Indeed a person passes through as an image; yet they are troubled in vain. He stores treasure and does not know for whom he will gather it.
And now, what is my expectation? Is it not the Lord? And my existence comes from Thee.
Rescue me from all my lawless deeds; Thou hast given me as a reproach to a fool.
I became mute and did not open my mouth, because Thou art the One who made me.
Remove Thy scourges from me; from the strength of Thy hand I wasted away.
With rebukes for lawlessness Thou didst discipline a person and melt his soul like a spider. Yet every person is troubled in vain. Diapsalma.
Hear my prayer, Lord, and give ear to my supplication; do not remain silent at my tears. For I am a sojourner with Thee and a temporary resident like all my fathers.
Give me relief, that I may be refreshed, before I depart and no longer exist.”
And a shoot will come from the root of Jesse, and a blossom will rise from the root.
And the Spirit of God will rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and godliness.
The spirit of the fear of God will fill him. He will not judge according to appearance, nor reprove according to report;
but he will judge the cause of the lowly, and reprove the lowly of the earth; and he will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with breath through his lips he will slay the ungodly.
His loins will be girded with righteousness, and his sides bound with truth.
And the wolf will feed with the lamb, and the leopard will rest with the young goat; and the calf and the bull and the lion will feed together, and a little child will lead them.
And the ox and the bear will feed together, and their young will be together; and the lion and the ox will eat straw together.
And an infant will stretch out his hand over the hole of asps, and over the nest of their young.

And they will certainly do no harm, nor will they be able at all to destroy anyone upon My holy mountain; for the whole earth has been filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as abundant water covers the seas.
On that day there will be Jesse’s root and the one rising to rule nations; nations will hope in him, and his rest will be honor.
For thus says the Lord: I Myself will take from the cedar’s choice parts, nip off from the top of their heart, and I Myself will plant it upon a high mountain. I will suspend it

upon Israel’s lofty mountain and plant it. It will produce a shoot, bear fruit and become a great cedar. Every beast will rest beneath it, every bird will rest under its shade, and its branches will be restored.
All the plain’s trees will know that I am the Lord who lowers a high tree, raises a low tree, dries a green tree and makes a dry tree flourish. I, the Lord, have spoken and will act.”
Lord, in affliction I remembered Thee; in slight affliction Thy discipline was for us.
Like a woman in labor nearing childbirth and crying out in her pang, so we became toward Thy beloved because of fear of Thee, Lord.
We conceived, labored and gave birth; we produced the spirit of Thy salvation upon the earth, but those dwelling upon the earth will fall.
The dead will rise, those in the tombs will be awakened, and those in the earth will rejoice, for the dew from Thee is healing to them; but the earth of the ungodly will fall.”
Go, My people, enter your inner rooms, shut your door, hide for a little, a very little while, until the Lord’s wrath passes.
For behold, the Lord brings wrath from the holy place upon those dwelling on the earth. The earth will uncover its blood and will not cover those killed.
a bundle of injustice. Ephraim—his sin is hidden.
Pangs like those of a woman giving birth will come upon him. This son of yours is not prudent, because he will certainly not endure amid the crushing of children.
I will rescue them from Hades’ hand and redeem them from death. Where is your punishment, Death? Where is your sting, Hades? Consolation is hidden from My eyes.

Because this one will make a division among brothers. The Lord will bring a scorching wind from the wilderness upon him and dry up his channels and desolate his springs; it will dry his land and all his desirable vessels.
For I set all this upon my heart, and my heart saw all this: the righteous, the wise and their works are in God’s hand. A person knows neither love nor hatred; everything lies before them.

There is futility in everything: one event comes to the righteous and the ungodly, to the good and the bad, to the clean and the unclean, to the one who sacrifices and the one who does not sacrifice. As the good person, so the sinner; as the one who swears, so the one who fears an oath.

This is an evil in all that is done under the sun: one event comes to everyone. Moreover, the heart of human beings is full of evil, and delirium is in their heart during their lives; afterward they go to the dead.
Who shares with all the living? There is hope, for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
For the living will know that they will die, but the dead know nothing; they have no further reward, for their memory is forgotten.
Their love, their hatred and their envy have already perished; they have no further share for ever in anything done under the sun.
Come, eat your bread with gladness and drink your wine with a good heart, for God has already favored your deeds.
Let your garments be white at all times, and let oil not be lacking on your head.

Enjoy life with the woman whom you have loved, all the days of your futile life that have been given you under the sun, all your futile days; for this is your share in life and in your toil at which you toil under the sun.
Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your strength, for there is no deed, reckoning, knowledge or wisdom in Hades, where you are going.
The Lord created me as the beginning of His ways, for His works.
Before the age He founded me, in the beginning,
before making the earth and before making the deeps, before the springs of the waters came forth,
before the mountains were established, and before all hills He gives me birth.
The Lord made countries and uninhabited places, and the inhabited extremities of the world beneath heaven.
When He was preparing heaven, I was present with Him, and when He was marking out His own throne upon winds.
When He was making the clouds above strong, and when He was setting the springs of the world beneath heaven secure,
and was making the foundations of the earth strong,
I was beside Him, fitting things together; I was the one in whom He delighted. Day by day I rejoiced before Him at every time,
when He rejoiced after completing the inhabited world, and delighted in the children of humankind.
For from their small to their great, all have carried out lawless deeds; from priest to false prophet, all have done false things.
And they treated My people’s fracture with contempt, saying, ‘Peace, peace’; and where is peace?

They were put to shame because they failed, and even so they were not at all ashamed and did not recognize their dishonor. Therefore they will fall in their fall, and at the time of their visitation they will perish, said the Lord.
And the heaven above your head shall be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron.
The Lord give dust for the rain of your land; and earth shall descend upon you from heaven, until He wears you away, and until He destroys you.

The Lord give you over to slaughter before your enemies. You shall go forth by one way against them, and you shall flee by seven ways before them; and you shall be scattered among all the kingdoms of the earth.
And your dead shall be food for the birds of heaven, and for the beasts of the earth; and there shall be none to drive them away.
The Lord smite you with the Egyptian ulcer upon the buttocks, and with grievous scab, and with itching, so that you cannot be healed.
The Lord smite you with madness, and with blindness, and with bewilderment of mind.
And you shall grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and He shall not prosper your ways; and you shall be wronged and plundered all your days, and there shall be none to help you.
And when Moses had finished writing all the words of this law in a book, even unto the end,
he commanded the Levites who bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, saying,
Take this book of the law, and lay it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God; and it shall be there for a witness against you.
For I know your provocation and your stiff neck; for while I yet live with you this day, you have been provoking God: how much more after my death!
Gather unto me your tribal chiefs, and your elders, and your judges, and your recording officers, that I may speak all these words in their hearing, and call heaven and earth to witness unto them.

For I know that after my death you shall deal utterly lawlessly, and turn aside from the way which I commanded you; and evils shall meet you in the latter days, because you shall do that which is evil before the Lord, to provoke Him to anger by the works of your hands.
And Jacob ate and was filled, and the beloved one kicked; he grew fat, he grew thick, he grew broad; and he forsook God who made him, and departed from God his Saviour.
They provoked Me with foreign gods; with their abominations they embittered Me.
They sacrificed unto demons, and not unto God, unto gods whom they did not know; new ones, lately come, whom their fathers did not know.
You forsook God who begat you, and forgot God who nourishes you.
Light is for the righteous continually, but the light of the impious is extinguished.
Deceitful lives wander in sins, but the righteous have compassion and show mercy.
An evil person does evil things with insolence, but those who understand themselves are wise.
Property pursued eagerly with lawlessness becomes less, but one who gathers for himself with piety will increase; a righteous person has compassion and lends.
A voice says, “Cry out!” And I said, “What shall I cry?” All flesh is grass, and all the glory of man is as the flower of grass.
The grass has withered, and the flower has fallen;
but the word of our God remains for ever.
For thus the Lord said to me, “There will be security in My city, like the light of midday heat, and it will be like a dew cloud on a harvest day.”

Before harvest, when the bloom is complete and the unripe grape blossoms as its flower forms unripe fruit, He will remove the small grape clusters with sickles, remove the vine branches and cut them down,
and leave them together for heaven’s birds and the earth’s wild beasts. Heaven’s birds will gather upon them, and all the earth’s wild beasts will come upon him.
Woe to those calling evil good and good evil, making darkness light and light darkness, making bitter sweet and sweet bitter!
Woe to those who are discerning in their own judgment and knowledgeable in their own view!
Woe to your strong ones who drink wine and the powerful who mix strong drink,
who justify the ungodly for gifts and take away the righteous person’s right!

Therefore, as a stalk is burned by a fiery coal and consumed by a rising flame, their root will become like chaff and their blossom rise like dust. For they did not desire the law of the Lord Sabaoth, but provoked the utterance of the Holy One of Israel.

The Lord Sabaoth was enraged with wrath against His people, brought His hand against them and struck them. The mountains were roused, and their carcasses became like dung in the middle of the road. In all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.
If you do not return, He will polish His sword; He bent His bow and prepared it,
and in it He prepared instruments of death; He fashioned His arrows for those being burned.
Behold, he was in labor with injustice; he conceived trouble and gave birth to lawlessness.
He dug a pit and hollowed it out, and he will fall into the hole he made.
His trouble will return upon his head, and his injustice will descend upon his crown.
I will give thanks to the Lord according to His righteousness, and sing praise to the name of the Lord Most High.
But I am a worm and not a human being, a human reproach and an object of the people’s contempt.
All who watch me sneered at me; they spoke with their lips and shook their heads:
“He hoped in the Lord; let Him rescue him; let Him save him, since He desires him.”
But Thou, Lord, art my helper, my glory and the One who lifts my head.
With my voice I cried to the Lord, and He heard me from His holy mountain. Diapsalma.
I lay down and slept; I was awakened, for the Lord will help me.
I will not fear tens of thousands of people who together attack me all around.
Rise, Lord! Save me, my God! For Thou didst strike all who were my enemies without cause; Thou didst crush sinners’ teeth.
Salvation belongs to the Lord, and Thy blessing is upon Thy people.
Lord, do not rebuke me in Thy fury, nor discipline me in Thine anger.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak; heal me, Lord, for my bones were troubled,
and my soul was greatly troubled. And Thou, Lord—how long?
Return, Lord; rescue my soul. Save me for the sake of Thy mercy.
For in death there is no one who remembers Thee; and in Hades, who will give Thee thanks?
I grew weary with my groaning; every night I will bathe my bed, with my tears I will wet my resting place.
My eye was troubled from anger; I grew old among all my enemies.
Stand away from me, all who work lawlessness, for the Lord heard the voice of my weeping.
The Lord heard my petition; the Lord accepted my prayer.
The sacrifices of the impious are an abomination to the Lord, but the prayers of those going straight are acceptable to Him.
The ways of the impious are an abomination to the Lord, but He loves those who pursue righteousness.
And Cain said to Abel his brother, “Let us go out into the field.” And while they were in the field, Cain rose against Abel his brother and slew him.
And God said to Cain, “Where is Abel your brother?” And he said, “I do not know. Am I my brother’s keeper?”
And God said, “What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries unto Me from the earth.
And now you are cursed from the earth, which opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
When you till the earth, it shall no longer yield its strength to you. You shall be groaning and trembling upon the earth.”
My little children, I write these things to you so that you may not sin. And if anyone sins, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous,
and He Himself is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the whole world.
And by this we know that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments.
The one who says, “I have come to know Him,” and does not keep His commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in that person.
But whoever keeps His word, in that person the love of God has truly been brought to completion. By this we know that we are in Him.
The one who says that he abides in Him ought himself also to walk just as He walked.
And Moses called all the sons of Israel, and said unto them, You have seen all that the Lord did in the land of Egypt before you unto Pharaoh, and unto his servants, and unto all his land:
the great trials which your eyes have seen, the signs, and those great wonders.
And the Lord God has not given you a heart to know, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, unto this day.
And He led you forty years in the wilderness; your garments did not grow old, and your sandals did not wear away from your feet.
You ate no bread, and drank no wine or strong drink, that you might know that He is the Lord your God.
I will exult and rejoice in Thy mercy, because Thou didst look upon my humiliation; Thou didst save my soul from constraints
and didst not enclose me in an enemy’s hands; Thou didst set my feet in a spacious place.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am afflicted; my eye was troubled with anger, my soul and my belly too.
For my life failed in pain and my years in groaning; my strength grew weak in poverty, and my bones were troubled.
Beyond all my enemies I became a reproach, and greatly so to my neighbors, and a fear to my acquaintances; those who watched me outside fled from me.
I was forgotten from the heart like a dead person; I became like a lost vessel.
For I heard the reproach of many dwelling all around; as they gathered together against me, they planned to take my soul.
